observations.value: bilateral alveolar infiltrates with predominance in lower lobes and right middle lobe; more confluent in right lung, especially middle and lower zones; left lower lobe also involved; upper lobes relatively spared
patchy to confluent opacities with air bronchograms visible in right middle and lower zones on PA (Fig 1a) and lateral (Fig 1b); consistent with alveolar filling
no blunting of costophrenic angles; no pleural fluid
preserved lung volumes; no hyperinflation or volume loss

hypotheses.name: pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP)
hypotheses.basis: bilateral, symmetric, lower-lobe–predominant alveolar opacities with relative sparing of apices; 'crazy-paving' may be subtle on radiograph but classic for PAP; absence of restrictive impairment (per option B) would be atypical but not exclusionary—some PAP cases have near-normal spirometry early on

hypotheses.name: infectious pneumonia (e.g., bacterial, fungal)
hypotheses.basis: alveolar infiltrates with air bronchograms suggest infection; however, distribution is unusually bilateral and symmetric for typical community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, which tends to be lobar/unilateral

hypotheses.name: ARDS
hypotheses.basis: diffuse alveolar infiltrates could fit ARDS, but classic ARDS shows more homogeneous, peripheral/gravitational gradient and often reduced lung volumes; here volumes are preserved and upper lobes spared—less typical
